items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Percy and I were good friends, but so was Caffrey and I.

ctx.x: It seemed to me it was very good, but I wouldn't swear to him.

Well, Caffrey Dallas, boy, was one of the greatest I ever heard. And he used to play up here with Manuel in the band at the old roof corner. With Manuel Borreiro. Right. And he left here and he went to Dallas. He sent him to Dallas and of course he sent for his brother later on Percy. Percy and I were good friends, but so was Caffrey and I. Caffrey was a genius. He was just like John Moreira. I don't know if you ever heard of John Moreira. Sure. John Moreira to me was the greatest banjo player I've ever heard in…

So it may well have been him on that date. Yeah, I'm sure it does. I'm almost positive. You don't remember him being in the studio or anything? Yes, I do. You remember him being there? Yes, I do. Oh, well that's great. I'm glad to know.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: I have never heard another man play as much. That was Caffrey Dyeronsburg.

ctx.x: People tell us he was wonderful on the blues like Careless Love, but was he good on other things too, everything? Or what style did he have?

Well, as far as I can remember, I just would sit up there and I used to go up there and listen to those bands play. They used to play in what we call the buzzard roof in these dance halls. We had to go upstairs. Oh yeah, the balcony. Upstairs in the balcony. And I used to go up there just a kid and sit down. I'd sit next to Buddy and just listen to him play. As far as I'm concerned, he played everything. Of course, Manuel Perez was at the Roof Garden. And there he had a great banjo player with him. I have never…
Yes, George Dano talks about him, says he was wonderful. And the younger banjo player over there, he started in 1927. He talks about...
